one_liner: Ramp offers a REST API and official MCP server for spend management and approvals.
gating_notes: Sandbox available for non-accounts; partner program required for building integrations for other businesses.
oauth_details: OAuth 2.0 with Client Credentials and Authorization Code flows; uses HTTP Basic Auth for token exchange.

auth_methods.quote: Ramp uses OAuth 2.0. Your app gets an access token from `/developer/v1/token`, authenticating with its client ID and secret (typically HTTP Basic Auth)

primary_auth.quote: Ramp uses OAuth 2.0. Your app gets an access token from `/developer/v1/token`, authenticating with its client ID and secret (typically HTTP Basic Auth)

credential_access.quote: Don't have a Ramp account? Request a sandbox to start building right away.

api_type.quote: Canonical OpenAPI schema for the Developer API: [/openapi/developer-api.json](https://docs.ramp.com/openapi/developer-api.json).

api_breadth.quote: End-to-end build journeys that span multiple Ramp products. Connect agents to Ramp via MCP or the CLI. Read data, process approvals, make purchases.

existing_mcp.quote: Ramp does publish an official MCP server — the open-source ramp-public/ramp-mcp project and a hosted documentation server at mcp.ramp.com

critic_flags.note: The ramp-mcp repository is hosted under the ramp-public organization on GitHub and is described as an official open‑source Model Context Protocol server by Ramp. The documentation and blog posts from Ramp’s own sites reference this server, indicating it is an official product.
